raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Motivation

The vendored VSA-H3 Triton tile-64 block-sparse attention kernel is gated to Hopper and Blackwell (supported_capabilities = {(9, 0), (10, 0), (10, 3)}). The kernel runs correctly on sm80 (A100) as well, but Triton only lowers TensorDescriptor (TMA) loads on Hopper and newer. On sm80 the descriptor loads are silently degraded to synchronous tile loads with no cp.async prefetch, so every K/V tile load exposes its full latency and the kernel is several times slower than the hardware allows.

Change

Add a second implementation of the same attention that loads Q/K/V/O through raw pointers, and select between the two from the device compute capability. On sm80 the pipeliner can then issue cp.async for K/V; on sm90+ nothing changes.

  • runtime/layers/attention/backends/vsa_h3_kernels.py

    • new _attn_fwd_sparse_ptr: identical arithmetic to _attn_fwd_sparse, raw pointer loads instead of tensor descriptors.

    • new _use_pointer_loads(capability) (capability[0] < 9).

    • new _ATTN_NUM_STAGES_PTR = 2 — the pointer path is not TMA-prefetched, so the deeper descriptor pipeline does not help (measured optimum on the production DiT shape).

    • vsa_h3_block_sparse_attn_forward dispatches on the capability and gains a q/k/v contiguity check.

    • the sm100 tcgen05 kernel is now imported lazily inside the branch that calls it. Upstream had pulled vsa_block_sparse_sm100 in at module scope, which makes the Triton path unusable on any stack that does not ship the Blackwell-only JIT kernel even though the branch is never taken there.

    • the TMA kernel and its num_stages=5 tuning are untouched.

  • runtime/platforms/cuda.py

    • _VideoSparseAttentionH3BackendResolver.supported_capabilities gains (8, 0); the fail-closed error message is updated.

  • test/unit/test_vsa_h3_attention.py

    • test_pointer_load_path_selection, test_vsa_h3_backend_resolver_allows_sm80 and test_vsa_h3_module_imports_without_sm100_symbol (CPU-only).

Evidence

A100 80GB, capability=(8,0):

check | result |   |   -- | -- | -- | --   |   | _use_pointer_loads((8,0)) / ((9,0)) | True / False pointer vs TMA descriptor kernel | `max | Δ | = 0.000e+00` (bit-exact) pointer vs fp32 torch reference | `max | Δ | = 2.29e-03` (bf16 rounding)

End-to-end (FastH3 4-step, 1344×768 / 5 s, A100): the sparse path runs 59.6 s vs 85.0 s for the dense fa baseline.

Re-run after rebasing onto main (62ff466ac0): the module reproduces max|Δ| = 0 vs the TMA kernel and 37.60 vs 293.24 ms = 7.80× on the production shape, i.e. the rebase did not change sm80 behaviour.

Full e2e re-run of the PR-form module on A100 GPU 0 (the rebased vsa_h3_kernels.py swapped into the v0.5.20 overlay; the sm100-only symbol is stubbed for the run only): rc=0, 59.72 s end-to-end (denoise 42.04 s / decode 13.33 s) vs 59.59 s for the pre-PR patch-0003 build — a +0.2% difference within run-to-run noise — and the generated mp4 is bit-identical (MD5 e26c4926… in both). The capability-gated dispatch therefore reproduces the validated raw-pointer kernel exactly end-to-end, not just in isolation.

Deployed end-to-end (32aa25fee0, module sha256 3d00b489…, installed into the overlay by deploy_pr_kernel.sh, no stub): rc=0, 59.58 s (text 3.96 / denoise 41.90 / decode 13.31), mp4 MD5 e26c4926… — bit-identical to the patch-0003 reference, i.e. −29.9% vs the dense fa baseline (84.96 s) with the same output. A per-branch launch counter inside the real e2e confirms the sm80 branch is what runs: ptr=200, tma=0, sm100=0 (50 attention layers × 4 steps).

Accuracy note

VSA-H3 is a 90 %-sparse approximation, so its output is not bit-identical to dense attention (vs the dense baseline: PSNR 14.6 dB, audio corr 0.60). This gap is inherent to the sparsity, not to the load path — the pointer and TMA kernels are bit-exact with each other. The dense fa path remains the default; this PR only makes the sparse path available and fast on sm80, as an opt-in tradeoff.

Testing

  • pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vsa_h3_attention.py

  • ruff format --check, ruff check, isort --check-only

  • CI has no A100 runner, so the sm80 GPU path is covered by the standalone probe below rather than by CI; the two new unit tests cover the dispatch and the resolver gate on CPU.

 import triton.language as tl
 from triton.tools.tensor_descriptor import TensorDescriptor
 
-from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import vsa_block_sparse_sm100
-
 # BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N are structural, not tunable: the kernel indexes the top-k
 # list per BLOCK_M q-tile and addresses keys as kv_idx * BLOCK_N, so both must
 # match the granularity q2k_index and variable_block_sizes were built at.
 VSA_H3_KERNEL_BLOCK = 64
 
 # Pinned instead of autotuned: on B300 num_warps=4 wins at every sequence
 # length and num_stages=5 is within 0.5% of the best (7 spills); FastVideo
-# reports the same optimum for Blackwell.
+# reports the same optimum for Blackwell. The raw-pointer path used on sm80
+# measures best at num_stages=2 on the production DiT shape (H=56, D=128,
+# S=37760, keep=66); its loads are not TMA-prefetched, so the deeper pipeline
+# the descriptor path relies on does not help there.
 _ATTN_NUM_WARPS = 4
 _ATTN_NUM_STAGES = 5
+_ATTN_NUM_STAGES_PTR = 2
+
+
+def _use_pointer_loads(capability: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
+    """Whether to use the raw-pointer kernel for the given compute capability.
+
+    ``TensorDescriptor`` loads are lowered to TMA only on Hopper and newer. On
+    sm80 Triton degrades them to synchronous tile loads without ``cp.async``
+    prefetch, so the pointer kernel is used there instead.
+    """
+    return capability[0] < 9
 
 
 @triton.jit
@@ -101,6 +119,95 @@ def _attn_fwd_sparse(
     )
 
 
+@triton.jit
+def _attn_fwd_sparse_ptr(
+    Q,
+    K,
+    V,
+    O,
+    sm_scale,
+    q2k_index,
+    q2k_num,
+    max_kv_blks,
+    variable_block_sizes,
+    H,
+    N_CTX_Q,
+    HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Same block-sparse attention as ``_attn_fwd_sparse``, loading Q/K/V/O
+    through raw pointers instead of TMA tensor descriptors.
+
+    On sm80 Triton does not lower ``TensorDescriptor`` loads to TMA; they become
+    synchronous tile loads with no ``cp.async`` prefetch, so each K/V tile load
+    exposes its full latency. Raw pointer loads let the pipeliner issue
+    ``cp.async`` for K/V on Ampere. The arithmetic is the same as the descriptor
+    kernel, so the output is bit-identical (verified against the Hopper path and
+    torch SDPA).
+    """
+    q_blk = tl.program_id(0)
+    off_hz = tl.program_id(1)
+    q_tiles = N_CTX_Q // BLOCK_M
+    meta_base = off_hz * q_tiles + q_blk
+
+    kv_blocks = tl.load(q2k_num + meta_base)
+    kv_ptr = q2k_index + meta_base.to(tl.int64) * max_kv_blks
+
+    # Contiguous [B, H, S, D]: fold (b, h) into a single base offset.
+    bh = off_hz.to(tl.int64)
+    sd = N_CTX_Q * HEAD_DIM
+    q_base = Q + bh * sd
+    k_base = K + bh * sd
+    v_base = V + bh * sd
+    o_base = O + bh * sd
+
+    offs_m = q_blk * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    offs_d = tl.arange(0, HEAD_DIM)
+
+    q = tl.load(q_base + offs_m[:, None].to(tl.int64) * HEAD_DIM + offs_d[None, :])
+    m_i = tl.full([BLOCK_M], -float("inf"), tl.float32)
+    l_i = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M], dtype=tl.float32) + 1.0
+    acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M, HEAD_DIM], dtype=tl.float32)
+    qk_scale = sm_scale * 1.44269504  # 1/ln2
+
+    for i in range(0, kv_blocks):
+        kv_idx = tl.load(kv_ptr + i).to(tl.int64)
+        block_size = tl.load(variable_block_sizes + kv_idx)
+        kv_row = kv_idx * BLOCK_N
+        k = tl.load(
+            k_base
+            + (kv_row + offs_n)[:, None].to(tl.int64) * HEAD_DIM
+            + offs_d[None, :]
+        )
+        qk = tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))
+        mask = offs_n[None, :] < block_size
+        qk = tl.where(mask, qk, -float("inf"))
+
+        m_ij = tl.maximum(m_i, tl.max(qk, 1) * qk_scale)
+        p = tl.math.exp2(qk * qk_scale - m_ij[:, None])
+        l_ij = tl.sum(p, 1)
+
+        alpha = tl.math.exp2(m_i - m_ij)
+        l_i = l_i * alpha + l_ij
+        acc = acc * alpha[:, None]
+
+        v = tl.load(
+            v_base
+            + (kv_row + offs_n)[:, None].to(tl.int64) * HEAD_DIM
+            + offs_d[None, :]
+        )
+        acc = tl.dot(p.to(tl.bfloat16), v, acc)
+        m_i = m_ij
+
+    acc = acc / l_i[:, None]
+    tl.store(
+        o_base + offs_m[:, None].to(tl.int64) * HEAD_DIM + offs_d[None, :],
+        acc.to(O.dtype.element_ty),
+    )
+
+

     q: torch.Tensor,
     k: torch.Tensor,
